newsitem.title: USA: Clinton budget taxing equity swaps, stock lending.
newsitem.headline: Clinton budget taxing equity swaps, stock lending.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's five-year budget plan proposed expanding income taxed under Subpart F to include equity swaps and stock lending, although regular dealers in such markets would continue to be excluded.
The proposal would raise a projected $200 million over five years.
Currently, income from "notional principal contracts," or derivatives, referenced to foreign currency, commodities or interest rates, are included in Subpart F, along with lending of debt securities.

But income from equity swaps and stock lending "is indistinguishable on policy grounds from other types of highly mobile income already targeted by Subpart F," the administration said in its budget plan.

An "ordinary course of business" exception would exempt regular dealers -- who earn the lion's share of income from such activities -- in property, forwards, options, notional principal contracts and similiar financial instruments.
The proposal would take effect for taxable years beginning after the date of enactment.
